task: R8 the O(alpha^5) term of the leading three-photon coefficient: sources read
handling: Downloaded from arxiv.org into separate empty directories; TeX read in memory from the e-print archive by a script kept outside them (python -I); nothing extracted or executed.

sources.used_for: one-loop normalization (1.9); Ritus's two-loop weak-field coefficients (4.11): 40/9 and 1315/252 relative to one loop; magnetic expansion (4.15) gives 40/9 independently; self-dual closed forms (6.2), (6.6) give 25/4 for 4c1 - c2, which fixes 1315/252 given 40/9
states (FF)^2 -> (1 + 40 alpha/9 pi)(FF)^2 and (FF~)^2 -> (1 + 1315 alpha/252 pi)(FF~)^2, from Ritus, confirmed by Reuter-Schmidt-Schubert; gives no cross-section factor
gives the two-loop magnetic-field integral representation (eqs. Gammascalrenorm, Gammaspinrenorm in the TeX), not the quartic coefficients; not used for numbers

re_read.finding: their two-loop factor 186685/17514 for the unpolarized cross section equals 2 d2 - (40/139)(d1 - d2); the weights computed here give 2 d2 + (40/139)(d1 - d2) = 25555/2502 (note E4, Section 11.3)

not_read: Ritus's original papers (Sov. Phys. JETP 1975; Proc. Lebedev Inst. 168) are not available; the coefficients rest on the quotations above and the self-dual check.
